 The financial aid guide
 For students who are applying for federal aid for the first time, the process can be time-consuming and wordy. Here’s a step-by-step key in simple terms. 
 By Karen Creviston , Staff Reporter 
 • 
 Nov 18, 2026 
 For Fresno State students hoping to get financial assistance for the upcoming fall semester, the Free Application for Financial Student Aid or FAFSA is now open. Students can submit applications for financial aid for classes July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2028.  
 Although needing lots of information, students with their FAFSA login, tax information and social security number handy can complete the free application in about 15 minutes.  
 FAFSA is not only for federal student aid, the information is used by states, schools and private aid providers as well.  
 Step by step: 
 Go to the FAFSA website and create or login to an account. Students can then select to start a new form or edit an existing form.  
 To get started, select the academic year you are applying for which will be for classes starting before or after July 1, 2027. Students will then login using an email or username and once signed in, a student can start their application. 
 First, students must identify if they are a student or parent and provide identification information including address, date of birth, residency information and SSN. If a student has completed an application before this, previous information will likely be saved.  
 Next, a student will be asked to give consent to retrieve and disclose federal tax information. 
 By giving consent, FAFSA can obtain tax return information automatically from the IRS to help complete the application. This step helps keep the application process quick and easy for applicants.  
 Students must provide consent to be eligible for any federal student aid, even if they didn’t file a U.S. federal tax return. 
 Afterwards, students are then taken to a six step information questionnaire.  
 Section one  
 Personal background asks students circumstantial questions and the information is used to help verify their identity, residency and dependency status.  
 Students that are dependents must provide their parents information to determine how much money they will receive.  
 Section two  
 Demographic asks for background and family questions. This includes sex, race, citizenship status and if the applicant has received a high school diploma.  
 Section three  
 Finances will ask for tax information. Although the application itself asks for some financial information, much of it is completed electronically through the IRS Direct Data Exchange. Since tax information has already been directly into the application this step only involves a few income questions.  
 Section four  
 Colleges and career schools will ask what school(s) should the FAFSA information be sent to.  
 Section five  
 For applicants that are dependents must invite a legal parent or guardian as a contributor by providing their email. The application is not complete until the contributors complete their portion.  
 To complete the application, students will then review their application and agree to the FAFSA terms and conditions.  
 If students need help filling out their application the Fresno State Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships is available. FAFSA also has a help page for every step of the application.
